blocks.text: As a fluid moves through a pipe of varying cross-section and height, the pressure changes along the pipe. Bernoulli's equation is the fundamental equation of fluid dynamics that relates pressure to fluid speed and height. In deriving it we assume that the fluid is incompressible, non-viscous and flows in a steady-state manner. Consider the flow of the fluid through the pipe in time t (Fig. 5.16).

blocks.alt: A pipe runs from a wide part high on the left, through a bend, to a narrow part low on the right, above a ground line. On the left, pressure P1 pushes a yellow slice of mass delta m, length delta x1 and area A1 moving with speed v1 at height h1. On the right, an orange slice of the same mass delta m, longer length delta x2 and area A2 moves with speed v2 at height h2, and pressure P2 pushes back on it from the right.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.16: An ideal flow of fluid through a non-uniform cross-section pipe at different heights (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.16).

blocks.text: The force on the upper end of the fluid is P1 A1, where P1 is the pressure and A1 the area of cross-section at the upper end. The work done on the fluid by the fluid behind it in moving it through a distance delta x1 is W1 = F1 delta x1 = P1 A1 delta x1. Similarly the work done on the fluid at the lower end is W2 = -F2 delta x2 = -P2 A2 delta x2, where P2 is the pressure, A2 the area of cross-section of the lower end and delta x2 the distance moved by the fluid in the same time interval t; W2 is taken negative because this work is done against the fluid force. The work done is W = W1 + W2, or W = P1 A1 delta x1 - P2 A2 delta x2 ... (5.19). If v1 and v2 are the velocities at the upper and lower ends, W = P1 A1 v1 t - P2 A2 v2 t. From the equation of continuity (Eq. 5.18) A1 v1 = A2 v2, hence A1 v1 t = A2 v2 t = V (volume), so W = (P1 - P2) V ... (5.20). If m is the mass and rho the density, V = m / rho, so Eq. 5.20 becomes W = (P1 - P2) m / rho ... (5.21).

A part of this work is utilised by the fluid in changing its kinetic energy and a part in changing its gravitational potential energy: change in KE, delta KE = (1/2) m v2^2 - (1/2) m v1^2 ... (5.22); change in PE, delta PE = m g h2 - m g h1 ... (5.23), where h1 and h2 are the heights of the upper and lower ends. Applying the law of conservation of energy to this volume of fluid, (P1 - P2) m / rho = (1/2) m v2^2 - (1/2) m v1^2 + m g h2 - m g h1 ... (5.24). Rearranging Eq. 5.24, P1 + (1/2) rho v1^2 + rho g h1 = P2 + (1/2) rho v2^2 + rho g h2.

blocks.title: Bernoulli's equation
blocks.text: Bernoulli's equation is often expressed as P + (1/2) rho v^2 + rho g h = constant.
